answer: Stake-bonded identity with slow reputation growth works well. Each agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, and trust grows only through a long history of honest work, like a willow putting down roots over seasons, not overnight. An attacker can still spawn copies, but each copy needs its own deposit and history, so a thousand fake voices cost a thousand bonds plus months of waiting. Correlated signals are discounted too: a raven vouching only for its own flock, or wallets in one shale-thin cluster, earn little trust. Fakery becomes expensive, slow, and visible.
